answer: Because the counters live in the crystal ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. An operator running many aliases as a result pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the lagoon quota and the tundra admission check. Submission rate is limited to 7 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
